outcomes: Students will learn to assess children's development through observation, documentation, and reflection to guide curriculum and teaching. Students will use observational techniques to assess children's learning and development to plan curriculum.

Students will develop effective strategies to foster positive connections, support and inclusion of children, a variety of people, including families from different backgrounds, diverse cultural values, peers, and their community.

Students will develop the ability to design and implement anti-bias, inclusive, research based and play based curriculum that addresses the diverse needs of each child’s individual characteristics, special needs, including but not limited to their physical, social-emotional, linguistic, cognitive, health, safety, and creative development of children 0-5 years of age.
Students will demonstrate understanding and ability to evaluate current research in early childhood education and development.

Students will apply their understanding of theory and developmental characteristics of children, both typical and atypical, from birth to age eight, and how it inform best practices in early childhood education.
